papers.title: LIGHT signaling through LTβR and HVEM in keratinocytes promotes psoriasis and atopic dermatitis-like skin inflammation.
papers.did: Used mouse models deficient in LIGHT or its receptors LTβR/HVEM in keratinocytes, and single-cell RNA-seq of patient biopsies, to test the role of LIGHT signaling in psoriasis (PS) and atopic dermatitis (AD).
papers.found: Mice lacking LIGHT or its receptors were protected from imiquimod-induced psoriatic features, and LTβR deletion in keratinocytes also protected against allergen-induced AD features; LTβR and HVEM transcripts were strongly expressed in keratinocytes in both PS and AD patient biopsies.
papers.used: Genetic knockout mouse models, imiquimod-induced psoriasis model, allergen-induced AD model, single-cell RNA-seq of patient skin biopsies, and in vitro keratinocyte gene expression assays.
papers.why: Suggests that blocking LIGHT signaling could be a therapeutic strategy for both psoriasis and atopic dermatitis.
papers.anchor_quote: Mice devoid of LIGHT, or deletion of either of its receptors, lymphotoxin β receptor (LTβR) and herpesvirus entry mediator (HVEM), in keratinocytes, were protected from developing imiquimod-induced psoriatic features, including epidermal thickening and hyperplasia, and expression of PS-related genes.

papers.title: Chromatin structure and var2csa - a tango in regulation of var gene expression in the human malaria parasite, Plasmodium falciparum ?
papers.did: Used targeted DNA double-strand breaks to delete the var2csa gene and surrounding chromosomal region in Plasmodium falciparum, then characterized the resulting changes in chromatin architecture.
papers.found: Deletion of var2csa produced a net gain of interactions in sub-telomeric and internal var gene regions, indicating tighter heterochromatin clustering that disrupts coordinated var gene activation.
papers.used: Targeted DNA double-strand break gene deletion combined with RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, and Hi-C in Plasmodium falciparum.
papers.why: Reveals a mechanistic link between the var2csa locus, chromatin structure, and virulence gene expression switching, relevant to malaria pathogenesis.
papers.anchor_quote: We observed a net gain of interactions in sub-telomeric regions and internal var gene regions following var2csa knockout, indicating an increase of tightly controlled heterochromatin structures.

papers.title: Lineage-specific 3D genome organization is assembled at multiple scales by IKAROS.
papers.did: Used loss-of-function and gain-of-function approaches in B cell precursors and epithelial cells to test how the transcription factor IKAROS shapes 3D chromatin architecture.
papers.found: IKAROS-bound enhancers assemble long-range, megabase-scale interactions that override CTCF-imposed boundaries to build lineage-specific regulatory units, and ectopic IKAROS expression can reconfigure chromatin architecture in epithelial cells.
papers.used: Loss-of-function and gain-of-function genetic approaches paired with chromatin conformation mapping in B cell precursor and epithelial cell models.
papers.why: Provides a paradigm for how a single transcription factor can pre-configure genome architecture to guide and restrict lineage-specific gene expression during development.
papers.anchor_quote: Loss-of-function approaches in B cell precursors show that IKAROS assembles interactions across megabase distances in preparation for lymphoid development.

papers.title: Atypical B cells consist of subsets with distinct functional profiles.
papers.did: Performed single-cell sequencing of transcriptomes, cell surface markers, and B cell receptors in individuals chronically exposed to Plasmodium falciparum to characterize atypical B cell populations.
papers.found: Identified three previously uncharacterized atypical B cell subsets with distinct transcriptional and functional profiles that differ markedly in their ability to produce IgG upon T-cell-dependent activation.
papers.used: Single-cell multi-omic sequencing (transcriptome, surface markers, BCR) in humans chronically exposed to malaria.
papers.why: Clarifies conflicting prior findings on atypical B cell function and their distinct roles in chronic inflammatory immune responses.
papers.anchor_quote: We identified three previously uncharacterized populations of atypical B cells with distinct transcriptional and functional profiles and observed marked differences among these three subsets in their ability to produce immunoglobulin G upon T-cell-dependent activation.

papers.title: Brd2 is dispensable for genome compartmentalization and replication timing.
papers.did: Performed E/L Repli-Seq and re-analyzed prior Micro-C data following Brd2 depletion in a conditional degron mouse embryonic stem cell line to test its effect on replication timing and genome compartmentalization.
papers.found: Brd2 depletion caused no significant alterations in replication timing, and re-analysis of the Micro-C data found no detectable A/B compartmentalization changes, contradicting a previous report.
papers.used: Brd2 conditional degron cell line with E/L Repli-Seq and Micro-C re-analysis in mouse embryonic stem cells.
papers.why: Corrects the prior literature by showing Brd2 alone is not required for genome compartmentalization or replication timing.
papers.anchor_quote: We report that we were unable to detect any compartmentalization changes in Brd2 depleted cells compared to DMSO control using the same data.

papers.title: MuDCoD: multi-subject community detection in personalized dynamic gene networks from single-cell RNA sequencing.
papers.did: Developed MuDCoD, a spectral-clustering-based computational method for multi-subject community detection in personalized dynamic gene co-expression networks from single-cell RNA-seq data.
papers.found: MuDCoD effectively leverages shared signal among subjects' networks at individual time points and performs robustly even with little information sharing, enabling robust inference of time-varying personalized gene modules.
papers.used: A spectral clustering framework applied to scRNA-seq datasets of iPSC dopaminergic neuron differentiation and CD4+ T cell activation, implemented as an open-source Python package.
papers.why: Enables discovery of subject-specific and time-varying gene network dynamics important for understanding phenotypic differences between individuals.
papers.anchor_quote: MuDCoD builds on the spectral clustering framework and promotes information sharing among the networks of the subjects as well as networks at different time points.

papers.title: 3D genome mapping identifies subgroup-specific chromosome conformations and tumor-dependency genes in ependymoma.
papers.did: Used Hi-C, CTCF and H3K27ac ChIP-seq, gene expression, and DNA methylation analysis on primary and relapsed ependymoma tumors to map 3D chromatin conformations across molecular subgroups.
papers.found: Identified new 'neo-TADs' formed by structural variants, group-specific 3D chromatin loops, and CTCF insulator replacement by DNA hyper-methylation, and validated tumor-dependency genes essential for patient-derived model survival.
papers.used: Hi-C, ChIP-seq (CTCF, H3K27ac), DNA methylation profiling, and gene inhibition experiments in patient-derived ependymoma models.
papers.why: Reveals tumor-dependency genes via 3D genome conformation even in tumors lacking targetable genetic alterations, opening new therapeutic avenues.
papers.anchor_quote: In particular, we observe the formation of new topologically associating domains ('neo-TADs') caused by structural variants, group-specific 3D chromatin loops, and the replacement of CTCF insulators by DNA hyper-methylation.

papers.title: Rewiring of the 3D genome during acquisition of carboplatin resistance in a triple-negative breast cancer patient-derived xenograft.
papers.did: Integrated Hi-C, RNA-seq, and whole-genome sequencing on triple-negative breast cancer patient-derived xenograft tumors before and after acquiring carboplatin resistance.
papers.found: Resistant tumors showed increased short-range chromatin interactions, new TAD formation, chromatin state switching to a more active state, and amplification of ATP-binding cassette transporters, alongside increased ribosome biogenesis and oxidative phosphorylation.
papers.used: Hi-C chromatin conformation capture, RNA-seq, and whole-genome sequencing in a patient-derived xenograft model.
papers.why: Identifies 3D genome remodeling as a potential mechanism underlying chemotherapy resistance in triple-negative breast cancer.
papers.anchor_quote: We integrated chromatin conformation capture (Hi-C), RNA-seq, and whole-genome sequencing obtained from triple-negative breast cancer patient-derived xenograft primary tumors (UCD52) and carboplatin-resistant samples and found increased short-range (< 2 Mb) interactions, chromatin looping, formation of TAD, chromatin state switching into a more active state, and amplification of ATP-binding cassette transporters.

papers.title: Intermittent PI3Kδ inhibition sustains anti-tumour immunity and curbs irAEs.
papers.did: Conducted a neoadjuvant, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase II trial of the PI3Kδ inhibitor AMG319 in head and neck cancer patients, complemented with mouse model experiments testing intermittent dosing regimens.
papers.found: PI3Kδ inhibition decreased tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells and enhanced cytotoxic T cell activity, but caused immune-related adverse events requiring treatment discontinuation in 12 of 21 patients; intermittent dosing in mice reduced tumor growth without inducing pathogenic colonic T cells.
papers.used: A phase II clinical trial (AMG319), single-cell RNA-sequencing, and mouse tumor models with intermittent dosing regimens.
papers.why: Identifies an alternative dosing strategy that could preserve the anti-tumor benefits of PI3Kδ inhibition while limiting toxic immune-related side effects.
papers.anchor_quote: A modified treatment regimen with intermittent dosing of PI3Kδi in mouse models led to a significant decrease in tumour growth without inducing pathogenic T cells in colonic tissue, indicating that alternative dosing regimens might limit toxicity.
